## Student life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Nottingham&action=edit&section=26 "Edit section: Student life")]

### Students' union

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Nottingham&action=edit&section=27 "Edit section: Students' union")]

Main article: [University of Nottingham Students' Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Nottingham_Students'_Union "University of Nottingham Students' Union")

The University of Nottingham Students' Union is the [students' union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Students'_union "Students' union") of the university and is based in the university's Portland Building.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Nottingham#cite_note-121) It has more than 200 affiliated [student societies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Student_societies "Student societies") and 70 sports clubs.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Nottingham#cite_note-122)

The students' union publishes the magazine _[Impact](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impact\_(student\_magazine) "Impact (student magazine)")_ five times a year.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Nottingham#cite_note-123) It also has a radio station, [University Radio Nottingham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_Radio_Nottingham "University Radio Nottingham").[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Nottingham#cite_note-124) and manages the [Nottingham New Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Theatre_(Nottingham) "New Theatre (Nottingham)").[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Nottingham#cite_note-125) The union's [rag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rag_(student_society) "Rag (student society)"), "Karnival" (abbreviated to "Karni") set a European record for fundraising by a student-run group in 2012, raising £1.6 million for charity.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Nottingham#cite_note-126) The students' union also has a branch of the international volunteering charity, [InterVol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/InterVol "InterVol"), which places student volunteers locally and internationally.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Nottingham#cite_note-127)

### Sports

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Nottingham&action=edit&section=28 "Edit section: Sports")]

Nottingham has a strong reputation for sport and was named the _Times_ and _Sunday Times_ sports university of the year for 2019, 2021 and 2024.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Nottingham#cite_note-128)[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Nottingham#cite_note-129)[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Nottingham#cite_note-130)

In addition to competing in national [British Universities and Colleges Sport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Universities_and_Colleges_Sport "British Universities and Colleges Sport") competitions, Nottingham also participates in the annual [Varsity Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Varsity_Series_(Nottingham_universities) "The Varsity Series (Nottingham universities)"), a multi-sport series between Nottingham University and local rivals [Nottingham Trent University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nottingham_Trent_University "Nottingham Trent University").[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Nottingham#cite_note-131)

Nottingham also has an extensive [intramural sport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intramural_sport "Intramural sport") programme, with 4,000 students playing on teams representing halls, courses, societies and groups of friends.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Nottingham#cite_note-132) Nottingham intramural teams compete against Loughborough Hall Sports teams in the annual IMS Varsity.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Nottingham#cite_note-133) There are specific "Hall Sports Leagues" in football and netball for teams from university-owned halls of residence.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Nottingham#cite_note-134)

### Residential life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Nottingham&action=edit&section=29 "Edit section: Residential life")]

Nottingham historically had [junior common room](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junior_common_room "Junior common room") committees (elected from the student body) that organised social events for residents of university halls.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Nottingham#cite_note-135) However, as of 2025, social events in University of Nottingham halls of residence are instead organised by the university's residential experience team.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Nottingham#cite_note-136) The university's community engagement team supports students living off-campus in purpose built student accommodation or in private rental properties.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Nottingham#cite_note-137)

Sir [Peter Mansfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Mansfield "Peter Mansfield"), physicist who was awarded the 2003 [Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Physiology_or_Medicine "Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine")

[![Image 21](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8a/Clive_Granger_by_Olaf_Storbeck.jpg/250px-Clive_Granger_by_Olaf_Storbeck.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Clive_Granger_by_Olaf_Storbeck.jpg)

Sir [Clive Granger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clive_Granger "Clive Granger"), economist awarded the 2003 [Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Memorial_Prize_in_Economic_Sciences "Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences")

The university has been associated with a range of notable alumni and staff in a number of disciplines: Nobel Prize or Fields Medal winners include Sir [Clive Granger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clive_Granger "Clive Granger") – 2003 [Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Memorial_Prize_in_Economic_Sciences "Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences"),[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Nottingham#cite_note-Academic_highlights-138) Sir [Peter Mansfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Mansfield "Peter Mansfield") – 2003 [Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Physiology_or_Medicine "Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine") for contributions to [Magnetic Resonance Imaging](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnetic_Resonance_Imaging "Magnetic Resonance Imaging"),[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Nottingham#cite_note-Academic_highlights-138)[Andre Geim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andre_Geim "Andre Geim") – 2010 [Nobel Prize in Physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Physics "Nobel Prize in Physics") for the discovery of graphene,[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Nottingham#cite_note-139) and [Caucher Birkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caucher_Birkar "Caucher Birkar") – 2018 Fields Medal "for his proof of the boundedness of fano varieties and for contributions to the minimal model program".[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Nottingham#cite_note-140)

[Frederick Kipping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frederick_Kipping "Frederick Kipping"), professor of chemistry (1897–1936), made the discovery of [silicone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silicone "Silicone")[polymers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polymers "Polymers") at Nottingham.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Nottingham#cite_note-Kipping-141) Nottingham professor [Angus Wallace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angus_Wallace "Angus Wallace") refined the [brace position](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brace_position "Brace position") used in aircraft following the 1989 [Kegworth air disaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kegworth_air_disaster "Kegworth air disaster").[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Nottingham#cite_note-142) In 2015, the [Assemble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assemble_(collective) "Assemble (collective)") collective, of which the part-time Architecture Department tutor Joseph Halligan is a member, won the [Turner Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turner_Prize "Turner Prize") for art.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Nottingham#cite_note-143)

The **Air University (AU)** ([Urdu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urdu_language "Urdu language"): جامعہ فضایہ _Jāmiʿah Fazaiyah_) is a federally chartered public-sector [research university](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Research_university "Research university") in Pakistan. Established in 2002, its main campus is located in the capital city of [Islamabad, Pakistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamabad,_Pakistan "Islamabad, Pakistan"). The university has Four other functional campuses: the Aerospace and Aviation Campus at [Kamra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamra,_Pakistan "Kamra, Pakistan") and a campus in [Multan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multan "Multan") Campus in karian and another campus in Karachi.

The university offers [undergraduate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Undergraduate "Undergraduate") and [post-graduate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-graduate "Post-graduate") degrees in [artificial intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence "Artificial intelligence"), [business management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Business_management "Business management"), [computer science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_science "Computer science"), [cyber security](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyber_security "Cyber security"), [engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Engineering "Engineering"), [medicine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medicine "Medicine"), and [humanities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humanities "Humanities").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-Why_air_university-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-Timeline_of_AU-2) It is ranked among the country's top ten universities in the Engineering and Technology category by the [Higher Education Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Higher_Education_Commission_(Pakistan) "Higher Education Commission (Pakistan)") (HEC).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-HEC_rankings-3)

Air University is recognized by the HEC and accredited by the [Pakistan Engineering Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistan_Engineering_Council "Pakistan Engineering Council") and [Pakistan Medical Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistan_Medical_Commission "Pakistan Medical Commission"). It is a member of [Association of Commonwealth Universities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_of_Commonwealth_Universities "Association of Commonwealth Universities") of the [United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom "United Kingdom")[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-ACU_Members-4) and [International Association of Universities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Association_of_Universities "International Association of Universities").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-5)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_University_Pakistan&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The university was established in 2001 with the aim to promote science and technology in Pakistan with Air Marshal Qazi Javed Ahmed appointed as its founding chancellor.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto4-6)

In August 2001, a feasibility report regarding the university was submitted to then University Grants Commission (UGC, now HEC) for approval.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto4-6) Later, in November 2001, UGC done a detailed inspection of the proposed premises.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto4-6)

In April 2002, the feasibility report was revised based on the feedback provided by the UGC. Meanwhile, construction of the admin block was started.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto4-6)

In September 2002, the first batch was admitted and classes began.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto4-6)

In October 2002, the university received a charter from the [president of Pakistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Pakistan "President of Pakistan").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto4-6)

In June 2003, the prime minister of Pakistan inaugurated the university formally and made a contribution of Rs 20 million for the expansion of the university.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto4-6)

In February 2006, the construction work on the Institute of Avionics and Aeronautics was started.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto4-6)

In November 2008, Air Commodore Ijaz A Malik was appointed as the second vice-chancellor of the university.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto4-6)

In March 2011, a new sub-campus of the university in Multan was established.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto4-6)

In October 2014, Air Vice Marshal Faaiz Amir was appointed as the new vice-chancellor of Air University.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto4-6)

In January 2020, Air [Marshal Javaid Ahmed](https://pakistan.gov.pk/) succeeded Air Vice Marshal Faaiz Amir as the new vice-chancellor.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto4-6)

In February 2020, Air University Aviation & Aerospace Campus Kamra, located on a land of 50 acres in PAC Kamra became functional.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto1-7)

In April 2024, Air Marshal Abdul Moeed Khan HI(M) has been appointed as new Vice-Chancellor.

## Campuses, constituent colleges, and affiliated institutes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_University_Pakistan&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Campuses, constituent colleges, and affiliated institutes")]

There is one main campus in Islamabad, two other functional campuses are located in Kamra Multan and Kharian, and Another new campus is under construction in Islamabad.

### Campuses

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_University_Pakistan&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Campuses")]

#### Main Campus

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_University_Pakistan&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Main Campus")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/04/Air_University_Main_Campus%2C_Islamabad.jpg/250px-Air_University_Main_Campus%2C_Islamabad.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Air_University_Main_Campus,_Islamabad.jpg)

Air University Main Campus, Islamabad

The main campus is situated close to the Margalla foothills in the southeast of sector E-9 (PAF Complex) of Islamabad.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto15-8) The primary entrance is adjacent to the intersection of Agha Shahi Avenue (9th Avenue) and Khayaban-e-Iqbal (Margalla Road), opposite to E/9 Campus of Bahria University, Islamabad. Different departments have different buildings. Faculty of Electrical Engineering Department is the oldest one. The newest edition to the buildings is the faculty of Computer Science, C block functional since 2022.

#### Air University Aerospace and Aviation Campus Kamra

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_University_Pakistan&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Air University Aerospace and Aviation Campus Kamra")]

Air University Aviation & Aerospace Campus Kamra is a 50-acre campus located in PAC Kamra and aims to further research in aviation. The campus is being built in five phases with phase one being complete and functional since February 2020.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto1-7)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-9)

The facilities of the campus include a separate hostel for boys and girls hostels, a dining area, medical facilities, and sports arenas.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto1-7)

#### Air University Multan campus

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_University_Pakistan&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Air University Multan campus")]

Main article: [Air University Multan Campus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Multan_Campus "Air University Multan Campus")

Air University Multan Campus was inaugurated in 2011 by then [prime minister of Pakistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_minister_of_Pakistan "Prime minister of Pakistan"), [Yousaf Raza Gillani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yousaf_Raza_Gillani "Yousaf Raza Gillani").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-10)

In the first phase, the campus started its operations in a commercial plaza named "Khan Centre" at Abdali Road, [Multan Cantt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multan_Cantt "Multan Cantt"), with a total covered area of about thirty-three thousand square feet, and about 700 enrolled students.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto7-11)

Now, the Air University Multan Campus (AUMC) has shifted to a proper built campus on 25.5 acres of land located at Bahawalpur Road, Multan. Phase-1 of the project is completed, in which one academic block and one hostel block have been completed, whereas three more academic blocks, two more residential hostels, an auditorium and a student center are planned in the near future.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto7-11) khariyan campus

#### South Campus

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_University_Pakistan&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: South Campus")]

Another campus is in the construction phase in [Sector H-11/2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sectors_of_Islamabad#H-sectors "Sectors of Islamabad") of Islamabad. The campus will comprise seven academic blocks, two residential blocks, a new automated central library, an administration block, an auditorium, and a cafeteria.

In January 2020, then prime minister of Pakistan, [Imran Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imran_Khan "Imran Khan"), laid the foundation of the new campus. First academic block and hostel was completed by December 2022.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-12) In addition to its own campuses, the university has two constituent colleges and five affiliated institutes. The H-11 campus is functional as of October 2025.

#### Kharian campus

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_University_Pakistan&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Kharian campus")]

Air University Kharian Campus is located near Kharian in Punjab, Pakistan. It was established in 2024 and began offering undergraduate programs from the Spring 2024 semester.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-14)

## Academic profile

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_University_Pakistan&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Academic profile")]

### Faculties

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_University_Pakistan&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Faculties")]

#### Faculty of Basic and Applied Sciences

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_University_Pakistan&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Faculty of Basic and Applied Sciences")]

The faculty of Basic and Applied Sciences comprises two departments: the department of mathematics, and the department of Physics.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto14-16)

Recently, the Department of Mathematics has started a master's degree in [mathematical modeling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematical_modeling "Mathematical modeling") and [scientific computing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_computing "Scientific computing").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto14-16)

#### Faculty of Engineering

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_University_Pakistan&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Faculty of Engineering")]

The department of electrical engineering offers degrees in three areas: [electronics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronics "Electronics"), [telecommunications](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telecommunication "Telecommunication"), and power.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto12-17)

Moreover, the faculty of engineering also offers BS and MS programs in [mechatronics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mechatronics "Mechatronics") and [biomedical engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biomedical_engineering "Biomedical engineering").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto12-17)

It has also collaborated with national centers such as the National Institute of Vacuum Science and Technology (NINVAST) and the National Center of Physics (NCP) to further strengthen the students and faculty.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto12-17)

#### Faculty of Computing and AI

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_University_Pakistan&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Faculty of Computing and AI")]

The Faculty of Computing and AI (FCAI) offers bachelor's, master's, and Ph.D. programs in computing and [artificial intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence "Artificial intelligence") fields.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto10-18)

In 2019, the department was upgraded as the Faculty of Computing & Artificial Intelligence with three separate departments, including the department of Computer Science, Creative Technologies, Computer Games Design and [cyber security](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyber_security "Cyber security").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto10-18)

FCAI faculty members have been included among the world's top two percent researchers.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto10-18)

FCAI also offers certification programs of [Huawei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huawei "Huawei"), [Oracle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oracle_Corporation "Oracle Corporation"), [Microsoft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft "Microsoft"), and [CISCO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CISCO "CISCO") through its newly established academy named Air University Computing Academy.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto10-18)

#### Faculty of Humanities and Social Sciences

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_University_Pakistan&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Faculty of Humanities and Social Sciences")]

The Faculty of Humanities and Social Sciences offers bachelor's, master's, and Ph.D. degree programs in [linguistics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linguistics "Linguistics") and [literature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Literature "Literature").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto13-19)

The faculty also offers a bachelor's of science in [psychology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychology "Psychology") and a master's of science in [clinical psychology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clinical_psychology "Clinical psychology") and education subjects.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto13-19)

The faculty has also established joint ventures with other organizations such as the Social Sciences Research Centre (SSRC), in order to tackle the contemporary challenges of society.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto13-19)

#### Faculty of Aerospace Sciences and Strategic Studies

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_University_Pakistan&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Faculty of Aerospace Sciences and Strategic Studies")]

The department of Strategic Studies is a department of the Faculty of Aerospace Sciences and Strategic Studies which helps in policy building related to [geopolitical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geopolitics "Geopolitics"), [economic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economics "Economics"), and social areas.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto11-20)

The Department of Aerospace Sciences and Strategic Studies also offers master's degree in [strategic studies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strategic_studies "Strategic studies") to civilians and officers of Pakistan Air Force.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto11-20)

#### Institute of Avionics and Aeronautics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_University_Pakistan&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Institute of Avionics and Aeronautics")]

The Institute of Avionics and Aeronautics (IAA) is a research institute that provides research services in emerging fields such as aerospace propulsion systems, active and passive surveillance systems, communication systems, digital signal processing, guidance and control systems, fluid dynamics, microwave circuit design, and navigation systems.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-21)

#### Air University School of Management

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_University_Pakistan&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Air University School of Management")]

The Air University School of Management (AUSOM) is a graduate [business school](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Business_school "Business school") of Air University. It offers bachelor's, master's, and Ph.D. degrees in [accounting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accounting "Accounting"), [finance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finance "Finance"), [project management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Project_management "Project management"), [hospitality management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hospitality_industry "Hospitality industry"), and [human resources](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_resources "Human resources") (HR).[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-22)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto15-8)

### Research centers

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_University_Pakistan&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: Research centers")]

#### CPEC Research Center

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_University_Pakistan&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section: CPEC Research Center")]

In February 2018, the CPEC Center of Excellence was established at Air University School of Management, Islamabad.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto3-33) The research center was established with an aim to understand the importance and contributions of [export-processing zones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Export-processing_zone "Export-processing zone") (EPZs) in human welfare and particularly maximizing its potential in the post-CPEC scenario.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto3-33)

The center is also working with the [Ministry of Overseas Pakistanis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Overseas_Pakistanis_and_Human_Resource_Development "Ministry of Overseas Pakistanis and Human Resource Development") to establish a university in Islamabad, Pakistan.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto3-33)

#### National Centre for Cyber Security (NCCS)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_University_Pakistan&action=edit&section=25 "Edit section: National Centre for Cyber Security (NCCS)")]

National Center for Cyber Security was established in May 2018 with the headquarters at Air University, Islamabad.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto2-34) The center was inaugurated by then Federal Minister for Interior, [Ahsan Iqbal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahsan_Iqbal "Ahsan Iqbal").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto2-34)

### Library

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_University_Pakistan&action=edit&section=27 "Edit section: Library")]

[![Image 62](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/23/AU_Central_Library_inside_view_%281%29.jpg/250px-AU_Central_Library_inside_view_%281%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:AU_Central_Library_inside_view_(1).jpg)

Air University Central Library

The Air University Central Library is the main library of the university and houses about 15,844 volumes of the print collection.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto8-36) Additionally, the library also maintains an active subscription with fifty-one publications and seven newspapers.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto8-36)

The library is also a member of the HEC's National Digital Library Program which provides on-campus access to 22,000 electronic journals and about 140,000 e-books.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto8-36)

The library facilities include six discussion rooms, fifty-six study carrels, and seventy computers for research purposes.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto8-36)

## Office of Research, Innovation, and Commercialization

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_University_Pakistan&action=edit&section=31 "Edit section: Office of Research, Innovation, and Commercialization")]

In January 2011, the Office of Research, Innovation, and Commercialization (ORIC) was established at Air University, Islamabad on the directives of the Higher Education Commission, Pakistan. In August 2013, the registration process was completed.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto5-40)

The office has established linkages with stakeholders and has secured research grants from research funding organizations including, the British Council, HEC, Ignite, Pakistan Science Foundation, and Ministry of Science & Technology.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto5-40)

### Business Incubator Center

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_University_Pakistan&action=edit&section=32 "Edit section: Business Incubator Center")]

Air University Business Incubation Center (AUBIC) is currently under the developmental phase.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto6-41)

This center will provide various facilities to incubatees including a conference room, meeting room, separate workstations, and halls for seminars.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto6-41) It will provide networking facilities to entrepreneurs with potential investors and venture capital firms.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto6-41)

## International Cooperation Office (ICO)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_University_Pakistan&action=edit&section=33 "Edit section: International Cooperation Office (ICO)")]

International Cooperation Office is a department of Air University that helps in the internationalization of the university.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto9-42) The office works to form associations and academic linkages with international universities and colleges and signs memorandum of understandings (MOUs) on the behalf of university.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto9-42)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto-43)

AU has more than 80 formal and informal international linkages with international higher education institutes of the world.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto9-42)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto-43)

The **Air University (AU)** ([Urdu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urdu_language "Urdu language"): جامعہ فضایہ _Jāmiʿah Fazaiyah_) is a federally chartered public-sector [research university](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Research_university "Research university") in Pakistan. Established in 2002, its main campus is located in the capital city of [Islamabad, Pakistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamabad,_Pakistan "Islamabad, Pakistan"). The university has Four other functional campuses: the Aerospace and Aviation Campus at [Kamra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamra,_Pakistan "Kamra, Pakistan") and a campus in [Multan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multan "Multan") Campus in karian and another campus in Karachi.

The university offers [undergraduate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Undergraduate "Undergraduate") and [post-graduate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-graduate "Post-graduate") degrees in [artificial intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence "Artificial intelligence"), [business management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Business_management "Business management"), [computer science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_science "Computer science"), [cyber security](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyber_security "Cyber security"), [engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Engineering "Engineering"), [medicine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medicine "Medicine"), and [humanities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humanities "Humanities").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-Why_air_university-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-Timeline_of_AU-2) It is ranked among the country's top ten universities in the Engineering and Technology category by the [Higher Education Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Higher_Education_Commission_(Pakistan) "Higher Education Commission (Pakistan)") (HEC).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-HEC_rankings-3)

Air University is recognized by the HEC and accredited by the [Pakistan Engineering Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistan_Engineering_Council "Pakistan Engineering Council") and [Pakistan Medical Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistan_Medical_Commission "Pakistan Medical Commission"). It is a member of [Association of Commonwealth Universities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_of_Commonwealth_Universities "Association of Commonwealth Universities") of the [United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom "United Kingdom")[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-ACU_Members-4) and [International Association of Universities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Association_of_Universities "International Association of Universities").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-5)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_University_Pakistan&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The university was established in 2001 with the aim to promote science and technology in Pakistan with Air Marshal Qazi Javed Ahmed appointed as its founding chancellor.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto4-6)

In August 2001, a feasibility report regarding the university was submitted to then University Grants Commission (UGC, now HEC) for approval.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto4-6) Later, in November 2001, UGC done a detailed inspection of the proposed premises.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto4-6)

In April 2002, the feasibility report was revised based on the feedback provided by the UGC. Meanwhile, construction of the admin block was started.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto4-6)

In September 2002, the first batch was admitted and classes began.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto4-6)

In October 2002, the university received a charter from the [president of Pakistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Pakistan "President of Pakistan").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto4-6)

In June 2003, the prime minister of Pakistan inaugurated the university formally and made a contribution of Rs 20 million for the expansion of the university.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto4-6)

In February 2006, the construction work on the Institute of Avionics and Aeronautics was started.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto4-6)

In November 2008, Air Commodore Ijaz A Malik was appointed as the second vice-chancellor of the university.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto4-6)

In March 2011, a new sub-campus of the university in Multan was established.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto4-6)

In October 2014, Air Vice Marshal Faaiz Amir was appointed as the new vice-chancellor of Air University.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto4-6)

In January 2020, Air [Marshal Javaid Ahmed](https://pakistan.gov.pk/) succeeded Air Vice Marshal Faaiz Amir as the new vice-chancellor.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto4-6)

In February 2020, Air University Aviation & Aerospace Campus Kamra, located on a land of 50 acres in PAC Kamra became functional.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto1-7)

In April 2024, Air Marshal Abdul Moeed Khan HI(M) has been appointed as new Vice-Chancellor.

## Campuses, constituent colleges, and affiliated institutes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_University_Pakistan&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Campuses, constituent colleges, and affiliated institutes")]

There is one main campus in Islamabad, two other functional campuses are located in Kamra Multan and Kharian, and Another new campus is under construction in Islamabad.

### Campuses

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_University_Pakistan&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Campuses")]

#### Main Campus

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_University_Pakistan&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Main Campus")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/04/Air_University_Main_Campus%2C_Islamabad.jpg/250px-Air_University_Main_Campus%2C_Islamabad.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Air_University_Main_Campus,_Islamabad.jpg)

Air University Main Campus, Islamabad

The main campus is situated close to the Margalla foothills in the southeast of sector E-9 (PAF Complex) of Islamabad.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto15-8) The primary entrance is adjacent to the intersection of Agha Shahi Avenue (9th Avenue) and Khayaban-e-Iqbal (Margalla Road), opposite to E/9 Campus of Bahria University, Islamabad. Different departments have different buildings. Faculty of Electrical Engineering Department is the oldest one. The newest edition to the buildings is the faculty of Computer Science, C block functional since 2022.

#### Air University Aerospace and Aviation Campus Kamra

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_University_Pakistan&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Air University Aerospace and Aviation Campus Kamra")]

Air University Aviation & Aerospace Campus Kamra is a 50-acre campus located in PAC Kamra and aims to further research in aviation. The campus is being built in five phases with phase one being complete and functional since February 2020.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto1-7)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-9)

The facilities of the campus include a separate hostel for boys and girls hostels, a dining area, medical facilities, and sports arenas.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto1-7)

#### Air University Multan campus

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_University_Pakistan&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Air University Multan campus")]

Main article: [Air University Multan Campus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Multan_Campus "Air University Multan Campus")

Air University Multan Campus was inaugurated in 2011 by then [prime minister of Pakistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_minister_of_Pakistan "Prime minister of Pakistan"), [Yousaf Raza Gillani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yousaf_Raza_Gillani "Yousaf Raza Gillani").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-10)

In the first phase, the campus started its operations in a commercial plaza named "Khan Centre" at Abdali Road, [Multan Cantt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multan_Cantt "Multan Cantt"), with a total covered area of about thirty-three thousand square feet, and about 700 enrolled students.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto7-11)

Now, the Air University Multan Campus (AUMC) has shifted to a proper built campus on 25.5 acres of land located at Bahawalpur Road, Multan. Phase-1 of the project is completed, in which one academic block and one hostel block have been completed, whereas three more academic blocks, two more residential hostels, an auditorium and a student center are planned in the near future.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto7-11) khariyan campus

#### South Campus

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_University_Pakistan&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: South Campus")]

Another campus is in the construction phase in [Sector H-11/2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sectors_of_Islamabad#H-sectors "Sectors of Islamabad") of Islamabad. The campus will comprise seven academic blocks, two residential blocks, a new automated central library, an administration block, an auditorium, and a cafeteria.

In January 2020, then prime minister of Pakistan, [Imran Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imran_Khan "Imran Khan"), laid the foundation of the new campus. First academic block and hostel was completed by December 2022.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-12) In addition to its own campuses, the university has two constituent colleges and five affiliated institutes. The H-11 campus is functional as of October 2025.

#### Kharian campus

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_University_Pakistan&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Kharian campus")]

Air University Kharian Campus is located near Kharian in Punjab, Pakistan. It was established in 2024 and began offering undergraduate programs from the Spring 2024 semester.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-14)

## Academic profile

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_University_Pakistan&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Academic profile")]

### Faculties

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_University_Pakistan&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Faculties")]

#### Faculty of Basic and Applied Sciences

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_University_Pakistan&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Faculty of Basic and Applied Sciences")]

The faculty of Basic and Applied Sciences comprises two departments: the department of mathematics, and the department of Physics.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto14-16)

Recently, the Department of Mathematics has started a master's degree in [mathematical modeling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematical_modeling "Mathematical modeling") and [scientific computing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_computing "Scientific computing").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto14-16)

#### Faculty of Engineering

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_University_Pakistan&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Faculty of Engineering")]

The department of electrical engineering offers degrees in three areas: [electronics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronics "Electronics"), [telecommunications](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telecommunication "Telecommunication"), and power.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto12-17)

Moreover, the faculty of engineering also offers BS and MS programs in [mechatronics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mechatronics "Mechatronics") and [biomedical engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biomedical_engineering "Biomedical engineering").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto12-17)

It has also collaborated with national centers such as the National Institute of Vacuum Science and Technology (NINVAST) and the National Center of Physics (NCP) to further strengthen the students and faculty.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto12-17)

#### Faculty of Computing and AI

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_University_Pakistan&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Faculty of Computing and AI")]

The Faculty of Computing and AI (FCAI) offers bachelor's, master's, and Ph.D. programs in computing and [artificial intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence "Artificial intelligence") fields.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto10-18)

In 2019, the department was upgraded as the Faculty of Computing & Artificial Intelligence with three separate departments, including the department of Computer Science, Creative Technologies, Computer Games Design and [cyber security](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyber_security "Cyber security").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto10-18)

FCAI faculty members have been included among the world's top two percent researchers.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto10-18)

FCAI also offers certification programs of [Huawei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huawei "Huawei"), [Oracle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oracle_Corporation "Oracle Corporation"), [Microsoft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft "Microsoft"), and [CISCO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CISCO "CISCO") through its newly established academy named Air University Computing Academy.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto10-18)

#### Faculty of Humanities and Social Sciences

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_University_Pakistan&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Faculty of Humanities and Social Sciences")]

The Faculty of Humanities and Social Sciences offers bachelor's, master's, and Ph.D. degree programs in [linguistics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linguistics "Linguistics") and [literature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Literature "Literature").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto13-19)

The faculty also offers a bachelor's of science in [psychology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychology "Psychology") and a master's of science in [clinical psychology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clinical_psychology "Clinical psychology") and education subjects.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto13-19)

The faculty has also established joint ventures with other organizations such as the Social Sciences Research Centre (SSRC), in order to tackle the contemporary challenges of society.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto13-19)

#### Faculty of Aerospace Sciences and Strategic Studies

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_University_Pakistan&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Faculty of Aerospace Sciences and Strategic Studies")]

The department of Strategic Studies is a department of the Faculty of Aerospace Sciences and Strategic Studies which helps in policy building related to [geopolitical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geopolitics "Geopolitics"), [economic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economics "Economics"), and social areas.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto11-20)

The Department of Aerospace Sciences and Strategic Studies also offers master's degree in [strategic studies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strategic_studies "Strategic studies") to civilians and officers of Pakistan Air Force.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto11-20)

#### Institute of Avionics and Aeronautics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_University_Pakistan&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Institute of Avionics and Aeronautics")]

The Institute of Avionics and Aeronautics (IAA) is a research institute that provides research services in emerging fields such as aerospace propulsion systems, active and passive surveillance systems, communication systems, digital signal processing, guidance and control systems, fluid dynamics, microwave circuit design, and navigation systems.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-21)

#### Air University School of Management

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_University_Pakistan&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Air University School of Management")]

The Air University School of Management (AUSOM) is a graduate [business school](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Business_school "Business school") of Air University. It offers bachelor's, master's, and Ph.D. degrees in [accounting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accounting "Accounting"), [finance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finance "Finance"), [project management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Project_management "Project management"), [hospitality management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hospitality_industry "Hospitality industry"), and [human resources](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_resources "Human resources") (HR).[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-22)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto15-8)

### Research centers

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_University_Pakistan&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: Research centers")]

#### CPEC Research Center

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_University_Pakistan&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section: CPEC Research Center")]

In February 2018, the CPEC Center of Excellence was established at Air University School of Management, Islamabad.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto3-33) The research center was established with an aim to understand the importance and contributions of [export-processing zones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Export-processing_zone "Export-processing zone") (EPZs) in human welfare and particularly maximizing its potential in the post-CPEC scenario.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto3-33)

The center is also working with the [Ministry of Overseas Pakistanis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Overseas_Pakistanis_and_Human_Resource_Development "Ministry of Overseas Pakistanis and Human Resource Development") to establish a university in Islamabad, Pakistan.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto3-33)

#### National Centre for Cyber Security (NCCS)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_University_Pakistan&action=edit&section=25 "Edit section: National Centre for Cyber Security (NCCS)")]

National Center for Cyber Security was established in May 2018 with the headquarters at Air University, Islamabad.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto2-34) The center was inaugurated by then Federal Minister for Interior, [Ahsan Iqbal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahsan_Iqbal "Ahsan Iqbal").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto2-34)

### Library

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_University_Pakistan&action=edit&section=27 "Edit section: Library")]

[![Image 62](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/23/AU_Central_Library_inside_view_%281%29.jpg/250px-AU_Central_Library_inside_view_%281%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:AU_Central_Library_inside_view_(1).jpg)

Air University Central Library

The Air University Central Library is the main library of the university and houses about 15,844 volumes of the print collection.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto8-36) Additionally, the library also maintains an active subscription with fifty-one publications and seven newspapers.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto8-36)

The library is also a member of the HEC's National Digital Library Program which provides on-campus access to 22,000 electronic journals and about 140,000 e-books.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto8-36)

The library facilities include six discussion rooms, fifty-six study carrels, and seventy computers for research purposes.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto8-36)

## Office of Research, Innovation, and Commercialization

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_University_Pakistan&action=edit&section=31 "Edit section: Office of Research, Innovation, and Commercialization")]

In January 2011, the Office of Research, Innovation, and Commercialization (ORIC) was established at Air University, Islamabad on the directives of the Higher Education Commission, Pakistan. In August 2013, the registration process was completed.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto5-40)

The office has established linkages with stakeholders and has secured research grants from research funding organizations including, the British Council, HEC, Ignite, Pakistan Science Foundation, and Ministry of Science & Technology.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto5-40)

### Business Incubator Center

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_University_Pakistan&action=edit&section=32 "Edit section: Business Incubator Center")]

Air University Business Incubation Center (AUBIC) is currently under the developmental phase.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto6-41)

This center will provide various facilities to incubatees including a conference room, meeting room, separate workstations, and halls for seminars.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto6-41) It will provide networking facilities to entrepreneurs with potential investors and venture capital firms.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto6-41)

## International Cooperation Office (ICO)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Air_University_Pakistan&action=edit&section=33 "Edit section: International Cooperation Office (ICO)")]

International Cooperation Office is a department of Air University that helps in the internationalization of the university.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto9-42) The office works to form associations and academic linkages with international universities and colleges and signs memorandum of understandings (MOUs) on the behalf of university.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto9-42)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto-43)

AU has more than 80 formal and informal international linkages with international higher education institutes of the world.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto9-42)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_Pakistan#cite_note-auto-43)

Where your donation goes

 Accountability and transparency are core values at the Wikimedia Foundation. We manage funds and resources to ensure that every contribution supports our mission. We have earned the Platinum Seal of Transparency from Candid (formerly GuideStar), and Charity Navigator awarded us its highest rating. You can [read our most recent annual report](https://wikimediafoundation.org/annualreports/current/) for more information about our financial health. 

45% Investment in Technology 
Nearly half of our budget goes toward supporting the technology that powers Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects. We are constantly working to enhance the user experience for both contributors and readers, improve site security, and ensure reliable access to our websites globally. This infrastructure and product support sustain one of the top ten most visited websites in the world, all at a fraction of the cost of popular for-profit websites.

32% Support for Volunteers 
The global reach of Wikimedia projects is made possible by the hard work of volunteers from across the globe. We provide grants, legal support, and other resources to help build vibrant volunteer communities. Additionally, we promote community engagement through outreach initiatives and advocate for the growth and protection of free knowledge.

12% Allocation to Fundraising Efforts 
Donor support is crucial to sustaining Wikipedia and our other free knowledge endeavors. Our team is committed to efficient and effective fundraising throughout the year, ensuring that every contribution helps advance our mission.

11% General and Administrative Expenses 
Operational costs are essential for the smooth management and governance of the Wikimedia Foundation. These expenses help us recruit top talent and support staff around the world, empowering them to carry out the mission of the Wikimedia Foundation.

The **University of Technology Bahrain** (**UTB**) is a [Bahrain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bahrain "Bahrain")-based university. Previously known as AMA International University of Bahrain, the university rebranded in 2021 after the acquisition deal by GFH financial group in Bahrain. The university provides many programs in business, engineering and information technology and seeks to be one of the leading business and technology school across the [GCC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_Cooperation_Council "Gulf Cooperation Council"). It follows a trimestral calendar, in which a typical four-year collegiate education program under a semestral calendar is completed in three years and three months. The university offers a bachelor's degree in international business, business informatic, informatics engineering, mechatronics engineering and computer science besides the MBA program.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Technology_Bahrain#cite_note-1)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Technology_Bahrain&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The University of Technology Bahrain (AMA International University) opened in September 2002 after the AMA Education system brokered a partnership with the government of [Bahrain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bahrain "Bahrain") to establish the AMA International University in [Manama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manama "Manama"). In 2008 AMA International University moved to their new campus in Salmabad.

**Awarding:** AMA International University has been awarded by the Higher education council for the IA (Institutional Accreditation) In May 2019. This will allow GCC students to join UTB (AMAIUB) and be one of their students.

Where your donation goes

 Accountability and transparency are core values at the Wikimedia Foundation. We manage funds and resources to ensure that every contribution supports our mission. We have earned the Platinum Seal of Transparency from Candid (formerly GuideStar), and Charity Navigator awarded us its highest rating. You can [read our most recent annual report](https://wikimediafoundation.org/annualreports/current/) for more information about our financial health. 

45% Investment in Technology 
Nearly half of our budget goes toward supporting the technology that powers Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects. We are constantly working to enhance the user experience for both contributors and readers, improve site security, and ensure reliable access to our websites globally. This infrastructure and product support sustain one of the top ten most visited websites in the world, all at a fraction of the cost of popular for-profit websites.

32% Support for Volunteers 
The global reach of Wikimedia projects is made possible by the hard work of volunteers from across the globe. We provide grants, legal support, and other resources to help build vibrant volunteer communities. Additionally, we promote community engagement through outreach initiatives and advocate for the growth and protection of free knowledge.

12% Allocation to Fundraising Efforts 
Donor support is crucial to sustaining Wikipedia and our other free knowledge endeavors. Our team is committed to efficient and effective fundraising throughout the year, ensuring that every contribution helps advance our mission.

11% General and Administrative Expenses 
Operational costs are essential for the smooth management and governance of the Wikimedia Foundation. These expenses help us recruit top talent and support staff around the world, empowering them to carry out the mission of the Wikimedia Foundation.

The **University of Technology Bahrain** (**UTB**) is a [Bahrain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bahrain "Bahrain")-based university. Previously known as AMA International University of Bahrain, the university rebranded in 2021 after the acquisition deal by GFH financial group in Bahrain. The university provides many programs in business, engineering and information technology and seeks to be one of the leading business and technology school across the [GCC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_Cooperation_Council "Gulf Cooperation Council"). It follows a trimestral calendar, in which a typical four-year collegiate education program under a semestral calendar is completed in three years and three months. The university offers a bachelor's degree in international business, business informatic, informatics engineering, mechatronics engineering and computer science besides the MBA program.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Technology_Bahrain#cite_note-1)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Technology_Bahrain&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The University of Technology Bahrain (AMA International University) opened in September 2002 after the AMA Education system brokered a partnership with the government of [Bahrain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bahrain "Bahrain") to establish the AMA International University in [Manama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manama "Manama"). In 2008 AMA International University moved to their new campus in Salmabad.

**Awarding:** AMA International University has been awarded by the Higher education council for the IA (Institutional Accreditation) In May 2019. This will allow GCC students to join UTB (AMAIUB) and be one of their students.

Abu Dhabi University

**Abu Dhabi University (ADU)** ([Arabic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabic_language "Arabic language"): جامعة أبوظبي) is a private research university with its main campus in [Khalifa City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khalifa_City "Khalifa City"), [Abu Dhabi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi "Abu Dhabi"), [United Arab Emirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Arab_Emirates "United Arab Emirates"), and satellite campuses in [Al Ain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Ain "Al Ain"), [Dubai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dubai "Dubai") and [Madinat Zayed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madinat_Zayed "Madinat Zayed").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi_University#cite_note-4) Founded in 2003 by [Ali Saeed bin Harmal al-Dhaheri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ali_Saeed_Bin_Harmal_Al_Dhaheri "Ali Saeed Bin Harmal Al Dhaheri"),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi_University#cite_note-5) it is the largest private institution in the country that offers courses in various subjects up to post-graduation.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi_University#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi_University#cite_note-7)

## Overview

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Abu_Dhabi_University&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Overview")]

The university's inception can be traced to the Charter of Abu Dhabi University in the year 2000 by [Sheikh Hamdan bin Zayed al-Nayhan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamdan_bin_Zayed_bin_Sultan_Al_Nahyan "Hamdan bin Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan"), the-then [Deputy Prime Minister of the United Arab Emirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deputy_Prime_Minister_of_the_United_Arab_Emirates "Deputy Prime Minister of the United Arab Emirates"). Following three years of planning, the Abu Dhabi University was inaugurated in June 2003[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi_University#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi_University#cite_note-9) and opened its doors to students in September 2003. According to the university, its founders "envisioned an institution that would be among the best in the [United Arab Emirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Arab_Emirates "United Arab Emirates"), the [Arabian Gulf region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Persian_Gulf "Persian Gulf"), and the world".[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi_University#cite_note-ADU_in_Profile-10)

## Accreditation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Abu_Dhabi_University&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Accreditation")]

The College of Business Administration received AACSB accreditation in 2015 and [EQUIS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EFMD_Quality_Improvement_System "EFMD Quality Improvement System") in 2017.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi_University#cite_note-11) Some College of Engineering programs received accreditation from ABET in 2015. In 2016 the university gained accreditation from the Western Association of Schools and Colleges (WASC) in the United States.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi_University#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi_University#cite_note-13) The Bachelor of Architecture course at Abu Dhabi University (ADU) earned the Royal Institute of British Architects ([RIBA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Institute_of_British_Architects "Royal Institute of British Architects")) accreditation in 2018.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi_University#cite_note-14) Abu Dhabi University is a partner with CIMA who has been accredited through the CIMA Global Learning scheme.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi_University#cite_note-15) Abu Dhabi University is accredited by the [Commission for Academic Accreditation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commission_for_Academic_Accreditation_(United_Arab_Emirates) "Commission for Academic Accreditation (United Arab Emirates)") (CAA),[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi_University#cite_note-16) the UAE Federal Government's quality assurance agency for higher education.

Abu Dhabi University launched the 'ADU Smart Learning Center' to upskill faculty, design courses.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi_University#cite_note-17)

## Colleges and programs

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Abu_Dhabi_University&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Colleges and programs")]

Abu Dhabi University provides both [undergraduate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Undergraduate "Undergraduate") and [postgraduate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Postgraduate "Postgraduate") programs, and consists of four colleges along with an English Language Institute. It currently has 8,000 students from 70 countries.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi_University#cite_note-18)

## Campuses

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Abu_Dhabi_University&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Campuses")]

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/Abu_Dhabi_University_2013_03_13_%288582695329%29.jpg/250px-Abu_Dhabi_University_2013_03_13_%288582695329%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Abu_Dhabi_University_2013_03_13_(8582695329).jpg)

Abu Dhabi University

### Abu Dhabi Campus

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Abu_Dhabi_University&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Abu Dhabi Campus")]

Scheduled to open in August 2016, an expansion will also feature 12 classrooms, 110 faculty and staff offices, meeting rooms, and multi-purpose rooms.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi_University#cite_note-19)

### Al Ain Campus

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Abu_Dhabi_University&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Al Ain Campus")]

Main article: [Abu Dhabi University–Al Ain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi_University%E2%80%93Al_Ain "Abu Dhabi University–Al Ain")

Opened in 2003 as one of the oldest campuses of the university. In 2017, a new campus in Al Ain was scheduled to open by September 2019 at a $81M cost. The new expansions will feature 70 classrooms and 137 offices, providing capacity for more than 2500 students.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi_University#cite_note-20)

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/82/Abu_Dhabi_University_Al_Ain_Campus.jpg/250px-Abu_Dhabi_University_Al_Ain_Campus.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Abu_Dhabi_University_Al_Ain_Campus.jpg)

### Dubai Campus

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Abu_Dhabi_University&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Dubai Campus")]

Main article: [Abu Dhabi University–Dubai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi_University%E2%80%93Dubai "Abu Dhabi University–Dubai")

Abu Dhabi University opened a new campus in Dubai located in [Dubai Knowledge Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dubai_Knowledge_Park "Dubai Knowledge Park") in September 2017. The 3,490-square-metre campus was inaugurated by [Shaikh Nahyan Bin Mubarak Al Nahyan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheikh_Nahyan_bin_Mubarak_Al_Nahyan "Sheikh Nahyan bin Mubarak Al Nahyan"), Minister of Culture and Knowledge Development, who is also the vice-president of ADU's Board of Regents.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi_University#cite_note-21)

Abu Dhabi University

**Abu Dhabi University (ADU)** ([Arabic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabic_language "Arabic language"): جامعة أبوظبي) is a private research university with its main campus in [Khalifa City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khalifa_City "Khalifa City"), [Abu Dhabi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi "Abu Dhabi"), [United Arab Emirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Arab_Emirates "United Arab Emirates"), and satellite campuses in [Al Ain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Ain "Al Ain"), [Dubai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dubai "Dubai") and [Madinat Zayed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madinat_Zayed "Madinat Zayed").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi_University#cite_note-4) Founded in 2003 by [Ali Saeed bin Harmal al-Dhaheri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ali_Saeed_Bin_Harmal_Al_Dhaheri "Ali Saeed Bin Harmal Al Dhaheri"),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi_University#cite_note-5) it is the largest private institution in the country that offers courses in various subjects up to post-graduation.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi_University#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi_University#cite_note-7)

## Overview

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Abu_Dhabi_University&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Overview")]

The university's inception can be traced to the Charter of Abu Dhabi University in the year 2000 by [Sheikh Hamdan bin Zayed al-Nayhan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamdan_bin_Zayed_bin_Sultan_Al_Nahyan "Hamdan bin Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan"), the-then [Deputy Prime Minister of the United Arab Emirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deputy_Prime_Minister_of_the_United_Arab_Emirates "Deputy Prime Minister of the United Arab Emirates"). Following three years of planning, the Abu Dhabi University was inaugurated in June 2003[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi_University#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi_University#cite_note-9) and opened its doors to students in September 2003. According to the university, its founders "envisioned an institution that would be among the best in the [United Arab Emirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Arab_Emirates "United Arab Emirates"), the [Arabian Gulf region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Persian_Gulf "Persian Gulf"), and the world".[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi_University#cite_note-ADU_in_Profile-10)

## Accreditation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Abu_Dhabi_University&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Accreditation")]

The College of Business Administration received AACSB accreditation in 2015 and [EQUIS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EFMD_Quality_Improvement_System "EFMD Quality Improvement System") in 2017.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi_University#cite_note-11) Some College of Engineering programs received accreditation from ABET in 2015. In 2016 the university gained accreditation from the Western Association of Schools and Colleges (WASC) in the United States.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi_University#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi_University#cite_note-13) The Bachelor of Architecture course at Abu Dhabi University (ADU) earned the Royal Institute of British Architects ([RIBA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Institute_of_British_Architects "Royal Institute of British Architects")) accreditation in 2018.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi_University#cite_note-14) Abu Dhabi University is a partner with CIMA who has been accredited through the CIMA Global Learning scheme.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi_University#cite_note-15) Abu Dhabi University is accredited by the [Commission for Academic Accreditation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commission_for_Academic_Accreditation_(United_Arab_Emirates) "Commission for Academic Accreditation (United Arab Emirates)") (CAA),[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi_University#cite_note-16) the UAE Federal Government's quality assurance agency for higher education.

## ADU Smart Learning Center

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Abu_Dhabi_University&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: ADU Smart Learning Center")]

Abu Dhabi University launched the 'ADU Smart Learning Center' to upskill faculty, design courses.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi_University#cite_note-17)

## Colleges and programs

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Abu_Dhabi_University&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Colleges and programs")]

Abu Dhabi University provides both [undergraduate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Undergraduate "Undergraduate") and [postgraduate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Postgraduate "Postgraduate") programs, and consists of four colleges along with an English Language Institute. It currently has 8,000 students from 70 countries.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi_University#cite_note-18)

### Abu Dhabi Campus

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Abu_Dhabi_University&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Abu Dhabi Campus")]

Scheduled to open in August 2016, an expansion will also feature 12 classrooms, 110 faculty and staff offices, meeting rooms, and multi-purpose rooms.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi_University#cite_note-19)

### Al Ain Campus

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Abu_Dhabi_University&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Al Ain Campus")]

Main article: [Abu Dhabi University–Al Ain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi_University%E2%80%93Al_Ain "Abu Dhabi University–Al Ain")

Opened in 2003 as one of the oldest campuses of the university. In 2017, a new campus in Al Ain was scheduled to open by September 2019 at a $81M cost. The new expansions will feature 70 classrooms and 137 offices, providing capacity for more than 2500 students.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi_University#cite_note-20)

### Dubai Campus

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Abu_Dhabi_University&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Dubai Campus")]

Main article: [Abu Dhabi University–Dubai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi_University%E2%80%93Dubai "Abu Dhabi University–Dubai")

Abu Dhabi University opened a new campus in Dubai located in [Dubai Knowledge Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dubai_Knowledge_Park "Dubai Knowledge Park") in September 2017. The 3,490-square-metre campus was inaugurated by [Shaikh Nahyan Bin Mubarak Al Nahyan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheikh_Nahyan_bin_Mubarak_Al_Nahyan "Sheikh Nahyan bin Mubarak Al Nahyan"), Minister of Culture and Knowledge Development, who is also the vice-president of ADU's Board of Regents.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi_University#cite_note-21)
