## Disciplines

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Khulna_University&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Disciplines")]

### Agrotechnology

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Khulna_University&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Agrotechnology")]

The Agrotechnology Discipline at Khulna University was established in March 1996. The curricula cover all courses offered by the relevant institutions in the country as well as they incorporate Geographic Information System (GlS), Spreadsheet Analysis, and Computer Studies.

Agrotechnology Discipline also works with some modern technologies like biotechnology, tissue culture, genetic engineering, protected agriculture, heat stress mitigation, irrigation management, IPM (Integrated Pest Management), biological control (BC) of pests, etc. The discipline also collects and evaluates germplasm through its 'Germplasm Center'. The Agrotechnology Discipline has some new and ongoing technologies and varieties that are going to be released soon.

### Architecture discipline

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Khulna_University&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Architecture discipline")]

Architecture discipline is the second architectural discipline in Bangladesh and one of the first four disciplines opened at Khulna University, which formally launched its academic activities under SET School in 1991. The curriculum of architecture provides the students with knowledge of man, his society, his physical environment and the technological development around the world. The Bachelor of Architecture (BArch) program of the discipline is designed for five years. There is also an opportunity to earn a master's degree.

### Bangla language and literature discipline

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Khulna_University&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Bangla language and literature discipline")]

Bangla discipline was introduced in 2010–2011. It offers B.A.Hons. in Bangla language and literature. An MS program will be introduced soon.

### Biotechnology and genetic engineering discipline

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Khulna_University&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Biotechnology and genetic engineering discipline")]

Biotechnology and genetic engineering (the then [biotechnology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biotechnology "Biotechnology")) discipline launched its academic activities in 1995. In 2003, the discipline was renamed "Biotechnology and Genetic Engineering". The discipline offers a four-year professional BSc degree in biotechnology and genetic engineering and a two-year MS degree in biotechnology and genetic engineering.

### Business administration discipline

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Khulna_University&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Business administration discipline")]

The business administration discipline began in 1991. The university offers a 4-year bachelor's degree in business administration (BBA).[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khulna_University#cite_note-ba-about-us-20) The university has run management training programs for the Bangladesh naval officers since 1995.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khulna_University#cite_note-21) The school introduced a regular MBA program in 2002, and an Executive MBA (EMBA) program in 2005. BAD offers a contemporary quality admission process to have the finest students be a part of it & the university.

### Chemistry discipline

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Khulna_University&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Chemistry discipline")]

Chemistry discipline started in the academic session 2009–2010. It has a B.Sc. (Hons.) in chemistry program. It also offers M.Sc. in chemistry program.

### Computer science and engineering discipline

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Khulna_University&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Computer science and engineering discipline")]

In 1991, the computer science and engineering (CSE) discipline of Khulna University started its academic activities with 20 undergraduate students in Bachelor of Science in computer science and engineering. This discipline was the second of its kind to offer computer science/engineering education in Bangladesh after BUET.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khulna_University#cite_note-22) Since then around 600 undergraduate students (of 17 batches) have graduated from the discipline. A perfect 100% of graduates work in government and private organizations as well as in teaching professions at home and abroad. CSE discipline takes 40 students at the undergraduate level each year.

With support from the Ministry of Science and Information Communication Technology, the CSE discipline has run a postgraduate Diploma in Information Technology (PGD-IT) program since 2001. The discipline has achieved its target by producing around 200 PGD-IT professionals.

In 2011, the CSE discipline introduced an MSc.Engineering (CSE) degree. Students of MSc.Engineering (CSE) will benefit from the memorandum of understanding between the CSE discipline of Khulna University and the Department of Computer Science of the University of Saskatchewan, Canada.

Students of CSE have a computer club named Club for Updated Search on Computers (CLUSTER). CLUSTER arranges seminars, programming contests and publishes magazines.

### Development studies discipline

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Khulna_University&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: Development studies discipline")]

Khulna University is the second public university in Bangladesh that offers a Bachelor of Development Studies BSS (Hons.) program. Development studies discipline offers a four-year BSS (Hons.) in Bachelor of Development Studies under Social Science School. This discipline was introduced in the academic year 2011–2012. Development studies discipline now takes 45 students at the undergraduate level each year. Following the information of 2017, there are about six batches under the Bachelor of Development Studies BSS (Hons.) program. The first batch of this discipline is known as DS'12, sequentially DS'13, DS'14, and others. This discipline has a lot of achievements in extra-curricular activities (mostly in sports) among the inter-discipline events.

The development studies discipline has Bachelor's in development studies and master's in development studies programs.

### Economics discipline

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Khulna_University&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: Economics discipline")]

Economics discipline started its journey in 1999. Over the years, it has established itself as one of the economics learning institutions in Bangladesh. Graduates of this renowned discipline (department) are contributing to the field of education, research, government services and other private sectors.

The curriculum of this discipline has been framed by blending both theoretical and practical courses. The discipline is offering a four-year Bachelor of Social Science BSS (Hons.) in economics degree, 1.5 years of master's in economics degree and 1.5 years Master's in Development and Policy Studies (MDPS).

### Electronics and communication engineering discipline

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Khulna_University&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section: Electronics and communication engineering discipline")]

Electronics and communication engineering was offered in 1997 under the School of Science, Engineering and Technology (SET) of Khulna University. This discipline is the first of its kind in Bangladesh (i.e., it is the first discipline in Bangladesh that offers an undergraduate degree in electronics means of communication subjects as well as electronics). Besides the regular study curriculum, it conducts a project fair every year on World Telecommunication Day. The students bring their electronics-based projects to the fair. The best ones are rewarded. The discipline has a seminar library, a digital electronics lab, an electrical lab, an analog communication lab, a digital communication lab, a biomedical engineering lab, a computer lab, microwave and antenna lab.

ECE discipline offers a four-year BSc. Engineering. degree in electronics and communication engineering. Till 2015, 16 batches have completed their studies. In April 2012, the ECE discipline commenced an MSc Engineering. in the ECE program with a focus on electronics and communication engineering. PhD Programs in electronics and communications engineering have already been launched from the academic year 2016–2017.

Students of ECE have operated a club named "ROUTER" for Updated Search on ICT Based Technology. ROUTER arranges seminars, and project fairs, and publishes ICT-based magazines. ROUTER is the club of the students of the Electronics & Communication Engineering Discipline of Khulna University. Which elaborates as "Roaming Over the Universe Through Electronic Roadway." The theme line of the club is "In search of a new frontier."

### English discipline

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Khulna_University&action=edit&section=25 "Edit section: English discipline")]

Khulna University includes [English literature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_literature "English literature") and English language in its curriculum. English discipline came into existence in 1998, but the academic activities started in 1999. A language center was established. In Bangladesh, English literature is a celebrated curriculum preferred by the students. The discipline is [GPA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GPA "GPA")-oriented.

Under Arts and Humanities School, English discipline offers one undergraduate and two postgraduate programmes; one of the two MAs is MA in English, with courses in [contemporary literature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contemporary_literature "Contemporary literature") in English, [linguistics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linguistics "Linguistics"), and [literary theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Literary_theory "Literary theory"); the other is MA in the English language that teaches current theoretical and practical courses in English language and linguistics.

### Environmental science discipline

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Khulna_University&action=edit&section=26 "Edit section: Environmental science discipline")]

Environmental science as an undergraduate teaching programme is a relatively new one in this country. Khulna University opened the discipline in 1997. The subject incorporates physical, chemical and biological sciences, engineering and technology, socio-economics and management. The discipline offers a four-year undergraduate (Bachelor of Science in environmental science) and one and half years of postgraduate (Master of Science in environmental science) degrees and offers a Ph.D. programme.

### Fisheries and marine resources technology discipline

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Khulna_University&action=edit&section=27 "Edit section: Fisheries and marine resources technology discipline")]

The greater Khulna region, the southwest part of Bangladesh has been characterized by a blend of aquatic habitats; fresh, brackish and marine waters supporting a diversity of biological and physical resources. Situated a few kilometers away from the [Bay of Bengal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bay_of_Bengal "Bay of Bengal"), this region has [Sundarbans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sundarbans "Sundarbans"), the world's largest mangrove forest crisscrossed by creeks and canals.

Understanding the potential of such resources to the prospects of the country, the Fisheries and Marine Resources Technology Discipline was established in 1992 with a mandate to establish an avenue for research and academic programs in all aspects of fisheries for the second time in the country after [Chittagong University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chittagong_University "Chittagong University"). Chittagong University introduced undergraduate and postgraduate level education in Marine Science under the Institute of Marine Science and Fisheries (IMSCU) in the early seventies. Over the last fourteen years, the FMRT Discipline has experienced substantial growth resulting in a reputation for training and research, particularly concerning coastal aquaculture and mangrove ecosystems.

The course followed in the discipline has provisions for education in biology, ecology, culture and post-harvest fisheries. The course, in addition, involves socio-economics, statistics, GIS and [remote sensing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Remote_sensing "Remote sensing"), computer applications, etc. The teaching staff of the discipline possesses knowledge in fish biology, marine science, aquaculture, fisheries management, genetics and fish breeding, ecology, oceanography and post-harvest technology. The FMRT discipline is now preparing to launch Ph.D. courses in addition to BSc and M.S. ones.

### Forestry and wood technology discipline

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Khulna_University&action=edit&section=28 "Edit section: Forestry and wood technology discipline")]

Khulna University launched [forestry and wood technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forestry "Forestry") (FWT) discipline as a second university in Bangladesh, in 1992. It offers a four-year Bachelor of Science (Honors) degree in forestry and a one-year Master of Science (MS) degree in forestry. The discipline is close to the world's largest single-tract mangrove forest, [Sundarbans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sundarbans "Sundarbans"), and the forest-deficient northern region of the country where forest extension and social forestry programme are increasingly realized. Given this geographic consideration, the mission of the FWT discipline in education and research stresses mangrove forestry, social forestry, forest management, forest tree improvement and wood science and technology.

History and civilization discipline will start their journey from the academic year 2016–2017, offering a 4-year Bachelor of Arts degree (abbreviated as B.A. (Hons.)) in history and civilization.

### Human resource management discipline

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Khulna_University&action=edit&section=30 "Edit section: Human resource management discipline")]

Human resource management (HRM) is a newly introduced discipline at Khulna University. The discipline has begun a bachelor's program in the academic year 2015–2016.

### Law and justice discipline

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Khulna_University&action=edit&section=31 "Edit section: Law and justice discipline")]

Law and justice discipline is another new discipline of Khulna University, offering 4 years LLB(Hons) courses from the academic year 2016–2017. Their LLM program will start soon.

### Mass communication and journalism discipline

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Khulna_University&action=edit&section=32 "Edit section: Mass communication and journalism discipline")]

Mass communication and journalism (MCJ) discipline is a newly introduced discipline, commencing a bachelor's degree program in the academic year 2015–2016.

### Mathematics discipline

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Khulna_University&action=edit&section=33 "Edit section: Mathematics discipline")]

The mathematics discipline was opened in the academic session 1998–99, offering a four-year undergraduate course leading to the degree of Bachelor of Science (Honors) in mathematics, abbreviated as B.Sc. (Hons.) in mathematics and Masters of Science in applied mathematics abbreviated as M.Sc. in applied mathematics. This discipline also offers a Ph.D. program for researchers.

### Pharmacy discipline

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Khulna_University&action=edit&section=34 "Edit section: Pharmacy discipline")]

Most of the present-day medicines are directly or indirectly obtained from plants of local origin and those of the [Sundarbans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sundarbans "Sundarbans"), a large source of medicinal plants. Some of the reported medicinal plants enjoy their use in herbal preparation. However most of the plants need to be scientifically evaluated. To this end, Pharmacy Discipline started its academic activities in 1997 under Life Science School offering a four-year Bachelor of Pharmacy (Hons.) degree with an aim of proper evaluation of the plants of medicinal value available in the mangrove forest as well as of medicinal plants in the native southern region.

### Physics discipline

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Khulna_University&action=edit&section=35 "Edit section: Physics discipline")]

Physics discipline started its journey on 28 March 2010 with 38 students in its inauguration batch in the academic session 2009–2010. This discipline currently offers a B.Sc.(Hons.), M.Sc. in physics. This discipline is also enrolling students for M.Phil. and Ph.D. programs in Physics. This discipline achieved two gold medalists and many trophies, with five consecutive championships in a volleyball inter-discipline tournament.

Fermineff Team from this discipline participated in the International Theoretical Physics Olympiad 2020 and secured 15th position in the world and 1st position in the country.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khulna_University#cite_note-23) Additionally, another team from physics discipline won a silver medal in University Physics Competition 2019.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khulna_University#cite_note-24)

### Soil, water and environment discipline

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Khulna_University&action=edit&section=36 "Edit section: Soil, water and environment discipline")]

Established in 1999 as soil science discipline, it was renamed as soil, water and environment discipline in 2017. The course and curriculum provide graduates with knowledge in the fields of soil genesis, hydrology, soil physics, soil chemistry, soil biochemistry, soil microbiology, ecology and ecosystems, soil mineralogy, soil survey, land evaluation, soil erosion and conservation, sustainable land use, watershed management, irrigation and drainage technology, groundwater hydrology, agronomy, soil fertility and plant nutrition, and [soil management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soil_management "Soil management") and others environmental related courses.

The discipline offers a four-year undergraduate programme leading to the B.Sc. (Hons.) in soil, water and environment degree. In 2008, a Masters programme was started.

### Sociology discipline

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Khulna_University&action=edit&section=37 "Edit section: Sociology discipline")]

Starting in 2003, sociology is one of the prominent disciplines of Khulna University under the Social Science School. The discipline offers a four-year Bachelor of Social Science (B.S.S.) Honors in Sociology degree as well as 1.5 years Master of Social Science (M.S.S.). It also teaches students of almost all other disciplines of Khulna University to fulfill their course requirements.

### Statistics discipline

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Khulna_University&action=edit&section=38 "Edit section: Statistics discipline")]

Statistics discipline under Science, [Engineering and Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Engineering_and_Technology "Engineering and Technology") (SET) School is one of the new disciplines at Khulna University. It initiated its journey in the 2011–2012 academic session. At the undergraduate level, statistics disciplines offer majors in statistics and decision science which can be taken in BSc (Honors) degrees. At the postgraduate level, advanced courses majoring in statistics have also been offered.

The discipline is distinguished by the faculty's strong interest in the application of statistics to diverse areas such as public policy, economics, engineering, medicine and life sciences, law, and the social and behavioral sciences. The research areas which are mainly focused here include- Data Mining, Econometrics and Quality Control, Demography and Research Methods, Experimental Design and Inference, Sampling Techniques, Inferences and Multivariate Analysis, Time Series Analysis and Forecasting, Demography, Stochastic Process, Computer Package and Programming, Biostatistics and Reliability Theory, Health Statistics, Epidemiology, Bio-informatics, Environmental Statistics and so on.

### Urban and rural planning discipline

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Khulna_University&action=edit&section=39 "Edit section: Urban and rural planning discipline")]

The [urban and rural planning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_planning "Urban planning") (URP) discipline was the earliest academic discipline in the country to impart planning education at the undergraduate level and was established at Khulna University in 1991. It is one of the four disciplines with which Khulna University started its academic programme. The urban and rural planning discipline offers a four-year undergraduate degree in urban and rural planning. The discipline offers a master's degree programme in urban and rural planning.

*   Library: Seminar Library

*   Discipline Journal: Plan Plus

## Kazi Nazrul Islam Central library

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Khulna_University&action=edit&section=49 "Edit section: Kazi Nazrul Islam Central library")]

Kazi Nazrul Islam Central Library, Khulna University was established in 1987. Before, it was housed in Academic Building I, D block. The library room has a floor space of 5,000 sq. ft. (465 sq meters). The library has its building now. The reading room has accommodation for 125 students, 25 teachers and research scholars working simultaneously. Khulna University library has a collection of 25,000 reading materials, including 23,000 books and 200 bound volumes of journals. The university library has a computer network for communication with national and international universities and institutions through the Internet.

The library is linked with the Automation and Networking of Science Technology Libraries in Bangladesh (BANSLINK) a pilot project of the Ministry of Science and Technology, the government of Bangladesh and Bangladesh National Scientific and Technical Documentation Center (BANSDOC) is the executing agency of the Project. Khulna University is also linked with Bangladesh's Education and Research Network. (BERNET) Project organized by the University Grants Commission (UGC), Bangladesh.

The central library is a Wi-Fi hotspot.

## Khulna University Central Masjid

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Khulna_University&action=edit&section=50 "Edit section: Khulna University Central Masjid")]

Khulna University Central Masjid was inaugurated on 28 August 2020 by The then Vice Chancellor [Md Fayek Uzzaman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohammad_Fayek_Uz_Zaman "Mohammad Fayek Uz Zaman").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khulna_University#cite_note-26) The total area of the masjid is 14500 square feet, while 2000 people can be accommodated at a time. The construction design was done by Ali Naqi, former professor of Architecture Discipline, Khulna University. Later, Associate Professor Shaikh Md Maruf Hossain finalized the design. The Masjid occupies 1 acre of land, located near to Kotka monument. The male residential halls (Khan Jahan Ali Hall, Khan Bahadur Ahsanullah Hall, and Jatir Jonok Bongobondhu Shaikha Mujibur Rahman Hall) are also located in proximity to the masjid. It is a single-dome masjid. The dome is the largest of its kind in the Khulna region.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khulna_University#cite_note-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khulna_University#cite_note-28)

## Khulna University Central Temple

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Khulna_University&action=edit&section=51 "Edit section: Khulna University Central Temple")]

Khulna University Central Temple was established in response to the continuous demands of Hindu students of the university. It is situated in front of Aparajita Hall and Sir Acharya Jagadish Chandra Academic Building and beside the Lakeside walkway. The foundation stone of the temple was laid on 15 February 2013. Construction of the temple was started on 20 August 2015. It took 7 years and 7 months to inaugurate the long-awaited temple from foundation date. The main temple is about 1100 square feet and the temple compound is about 3,000 square feet. The then Vice Chancellor [Md Fayek Uzzaman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohammad_Fayek_Uz_Zaman "Mohammad Fayek Uz Zaman") inaugurated the temple on 24 September 2020.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khulna_University#cite_note-29) Hindu students of the university observe [Sarawsati Puja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saraswati "Saraswati") here every year. A magazine "_Panchami_" is published each year during the [Sarawsati Puja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saraswati "Saraswati"). Besides, [Krishna Janmashtami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krishna_Janmashtami "Krishna Janmashtami") is observed annually by the Hindu students.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khulna_University#cite_note-30) They also observe [Diwali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diwali "Diwali") every year lightening well lamp over the campus including Hadi Chattar, Main Gate. Additionally, Khichuri Prasad is arranged frequently by the Hindu students of the university.

The **African Institute for Mathematical Sciences** (**AIMS**) is a pan-African network of postgraduate schools teaching mathematical sciences. Established in 2003 in Cape Town, South Africa, AIMS offers postgraduate training, research, and public engagement programs aimed at building scientific capacity across Africa. The institute was founded by physicist [Neil Turok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Turok "Neil Turok") to educate African students in STEM fields to support the continent's development.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-1)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

### Founder

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Founder")]

The first African Institute for Mathematical Sciences was founded in [Muizenberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muizenberg "Muizenberg") near Cape Town by [Neil Turok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Turok "Neil Turok") in 2003, while he was Chair of Mathematical Physics at [Cambridge University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cambridge_University "Cambridge University"). Neil Turok is the son of [Ben Turok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Turok "Ben Turok"), an [ANC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_National_Congress "African National Congress") MP. In 2008 Turok became Executive Director of the [Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perimeter_Institute_for_Theoretical_Physics "Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics"), and was replaced by Dr [Robert Myers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Myers_(physicist) "Robert Myers (physicist)") in 2019.

AIMS South Africa was formed as a partnership between the following universities: [University of Stellenbosch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stellenbosch_University "Stellenbosch University"), [University of Cambridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Cambridge "University of Cambridge"), [University of Cape Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Cape_Town "University of Cape Town"), [University of Oxford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Oxford "University of Oxford"), [University of Paris-Sud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Paris-Sud "University of Paris-Sud"), and [University of the Western Cape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_the_Western_Cape "University of the Western Cape").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-2)

### AIMS Next Einstein Initiative

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: AIMS Next Einstein Initiative")]

AIMS was the subject of a talk[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-3) by [Neil Turok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Turok "Neil Turok") after he received the [TED Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TED_Prize "TED Prize") in 2008.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-4) Neil Turok's TED wish was that, within his lifetime, an African Einstein would be celebrated.

The AIMS Next Einstein Initiative[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-5) is a plan to create 15 more AIMS centres across Africa. These centres intend to create institutions that are equipped with educational and scientific resources equivalent to the more developed continents, in order to fulfil Neil Turok's TED wish.

The first three centres created after that in South Africa are in Senegal,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-6) Ghana[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-AIMS-Ghana-7) and Cameroon. AIMS Senegal became operational in September, 2011 in [Mbour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M'Bour "M'Bour"), near [Dakar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dakar "Dakar"), and AIMS Ghana opened its doors in 2012 in the small coastal city of [Biriwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biriwa "Biriwa"). An earlier centre based at the [African University of Science and Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_University_of_Science_and_Technology "African University of Science and Technology") (AUST[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-8)) in Nigeria was known as AIMS [Abuja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abuja "Abuja")[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-10) for a while. AIMS Ghana was set up in 2012, AIMS [Cameroon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameroon "Cameroon") in 2013 and AIMS [Tanzania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanzania "Tanzania") in 2014. There is a sixth centre in [Rwanda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rwanda "Rwanda").

The AIMS Next Einstein Initiative is a continuation of the work of the African Mathematical Institutes Network (AMI-Net).[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-11)

After AIMS [South Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Africa "South Africa") won the TED Prize in 2008, Neil Turok and his partners developed the AIMS Next Einstein Initiative, the goal of which is to build 15 centres of excellence across [Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Africa "Africa") by 2023. The Government of [Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada "Canada") made a US$20 million investment in the Next Einstein Initiative in 2010, through its [International Development Research Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Development_Research_Centre "International Development Research Centre"), and numerous governments in Africa and Europe have followed suit. In October 2015, a forum took place in [Dakar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dakar "Dakar") under the auspices of UNESCO's International Basic Sciences Programme to take the project for a vast network of centres to the next stage.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-:13-12)

## Mission

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Mission")]

### Teaching and research

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Teaching and research")]

The AIMS institutes teach both basic and applied mathematics, covering a large range of mathematical applications in physics (including astrophysics and cosmology), quantitative biology, [bioinformatics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bioinformatics "Bioinformatics"), scientific computing, finance, agriculture modelling and so on. That in [Senegal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senegal "Senegal") proposes courses in both French and English.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-:13-12) In addition to its academic programmes, AIMS [South Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Africa "South Africa") has a research centre in interdisciplinary areas like cosmology, computing and finance (see below). In 2015, AIMS [Cameroon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameroon "Cameroon") was planning to launch its own research centre to host resident and visiting researchers from universities in [Cameroon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameroon "Cameroon") and beyond.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-:13-12)

### Community service

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Community service")]

The AIMS institutes provide community services. AIMS Senegal has developed an innovative teaching module for secondary school maths teachers and has partnered with local businesses to raise funds for the creation of a national contest on computer applications and mathematical modelling, with a focus on finding development-oriented solutions. AIMS [South Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Africa "South Africa") directs the AIMS Schools Enrichment Centre for primary and secondary school teachers, which also organizes public lectures, workshops and master classes and supports maths clubs in schools across the country (see below). Scholars and lecturers from AIMS Ghana have equipped teachers at [Biriwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biriwa "Biriwa") Junior High School with an innovative teaching module.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-:13-12)

## AIMS South Africa

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: AIMS South Africa")]

### Academic programme

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Academic programme")]

#### Structured Masters programme

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Structured Masters programme")]

The flagship programme of AIMS [South Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Africa "South Africa") is a 10-month Structured Masters programme in the Mathematical Sciences. The programme was upgraded in 2012 from a Postgraduate Diploma. The master's degree is conferred by the three South African universities in the partnership. Students from Africa can apply for full scholarships, including travel, board & lodging, tuition, and a stipend. AIMS is committed to greater participation by women in science and a geographically representative student body from the African continent.

Visiting faculty have included [David MacKay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_J._C._MacKay "David J. C. MacKay"), [Bernt Øksendal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernt_%C3%98ksendal "Bernt Øksendal"), David Aschman ([Cape Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Cape_Town "University of Cape Town")), Alan Beardon ([Cambridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Cambridge "University of Cambridge")), Jordi Campos ([Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Barcelona "University of Barcelona")), Jesus Cerquides ([Spanish National Research Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_National_Research_Council "Spanish National Research Council")), Patrick Dorey ([Durham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durham_University "Durham University")), Pedro Ferreira ([Oxford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxford_University "Oxford University")), Jan Govaerts ([Leuven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katholieke_Universiteit_Leuven "Katholieke Universiteit Leuven")), Barry Green ([Stellenbosch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Stellenbosch "University of Stellenbosch")), Gordon Johnson ([Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Houston "University of Houston")), Dirk Laurie ([Stellenbosch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Stellenbosch "University of Stellenbosch")), Sanjoy Mahajan ([MIT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MIT "MIT"), [Olin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franklin_W._Olin_College_of_Engineering "Franklin W. Olin College of Engineering")), [Vincent Rivasseau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vincent_Rivasseau "Vincent Rivasseau") ([University of Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Paris "University of Paris")), Bernd Schroers ([Heriot-Watt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heriot-Watt_University "Heriot-Watt University")), Robert de Mello Koch ([Witwatersrand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_the_Witwatersrand "University of the Witwatersrand")), Rob Beezer ([University of Puget Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Puget_Sound "University of Puget Sound")), Jeff Sanders ([United Nations University International Institute for Software Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_University_International_Institute_for_Software_Technology "United Nations University International Institute for Software Technology")), and [Tadashi Tokieda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tadashi_Tokieda "Tadashi Tokieda") ([Stanford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanford "Stanford")). Each visiting lecturer teaches an intensive three-week-long module.

The goal of the programme is to produce students capable of doing a high quality research-based master's degree. Special emphasis is placed on intuitive understanding, problem solving skills, collaboration, scientific writing skills, and computer modelling using [Free Software](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_Software "Free Software") such as [SageMath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SageMath "SageMath"), [SciPy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SciPy "SciPy"), and [R](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R_(programming_language) "R (programming language)").

AIMS offers scholarships for many alumni continuing studies in South Africa.

#### Honours Degree in Mathematical Biology

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Honours Degree in Mathematical Biology")]

AIMS, in conjunction with [University of Stellenbosch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stellenbosch_University "Stellenbosch University"), offers an honours degree in [Mathematical Biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematical_and_theoretical_biology "Mathematical and theoretical biology") for South African students.

#### Honours Degree in Mathematical Finance

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Honours Degree in Mathematical Finance")]

An honours degree in [Mathematical Finance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematical_finance "Mathematical finance") is being offered for South African students in conjunction with [University of Stellenbosch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stellenbosch_University "Stellenbosch University") and the [University of Cape Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Cape_Town "University of Cape Town").

#### Master's and doctoral studies

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Master's and doctoral studies")]

In the AIMS Research Centre students, often AIMS alumni, study towards a MSc or PhD degree under supervision of a resident researcher in [Mathematical Biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematical_and_theoretical_biology "Mathematical and theoretical biology") and [Mathematical Finance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematical_finance "Mathematical finance").

### Research centre

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Research centre")]

AIMS [South Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Africa "South Africa") hosts a research centre that opened in May 2008. [Stephen Hawking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Hawking "Stephen Hawking") visited the AIMS research centre and AIMS-Next Einstein Initiative launch.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-14)

The centre specialises in [Mathematical Biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematical_and_theoretical_biology "Mathematical and theoretical biology"), [Industrial Mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Applied_mathematics "Applied mathematics"), [Mathematical Finance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematical_finance "Mathematical finance"), [Astrophysics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astrophysics "Astrophysics")&[Cosmology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physical_cosmology "Physical cosmology"),[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-15) and [Computer Algebra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_algebra_system "Computer algebra system"). Bursaries are offered for Master's and doctoral studies.

### School Enrichment Centre

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: School Enrichment Centre")]

AIMS South Africa hosts a School Enrichment Centre which offers free learning resources and professional development courses for South African mathematics teachers.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-16)

### Workshops and conferences

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Workshops and conferences")]

AIMS South Africa regularly hosts short conferences or workshops in mathematics and its applications, especially in [physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physics "Physics"), [mathematical finance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematical_finance "Mathematical finance"), [epidemiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epidemiology "Epidemiology"). Other topics include [scientific modelling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_modelling "Scientific modelling") or [system administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/System_administration "System administration") using [Debian GNU/Linux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Debian "Debian")[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-17) as a platform.

### Public lectures

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Public lectures")]

Regular public lectures[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-18) on a wide range of topics are offered by [eminent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eminent_domain "Eminent domain") scientists at the forefront of research in their field.

### Funding

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Funding")]

AIMS South Africa is sponsored by international corporations, international development organisations and the South African departments of [Education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Education_(South_Africa) "Department of Education (South Africa)") and [Science and Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Science_and_Technology_(South_Africa) "Department of Science and Technology (South Africa)"). In February 2010, [Google](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google "Google") donated $1 million to AIMS.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-19)

In July 2010, Canada committed CAN$20 million of federal funding to AIMS and the AIMS-Next Einstein Initiative.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-22) The funds are administered by the [International Development Research Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Development_Research_Centre "International Development Research Centre") and the [Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perimeter_Institute_for_Theoretical_Physics "Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics").

In September 2010, the AIMS Next Einstein Initiative AIMS-NEI was awarded US$2 million from [Google](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google "Google")'s Project 10^100.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-23)

Individuals donate to AIMS on GivenGain.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-24)

## AIMS Ghana

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: AIMS Ghana")]

AIMS Ghana is among the oldest AIMS centers.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-AIMS-Ghana-7) Located in West Africa, initially based within the [University of Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Ghana "University of Ghana") in East-Legon, then based in the idyllic village of Biriwa in the Central Region, and then moved to [Accra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accra "Accra"). The center has been highly patronized by the figure of [Francis Allotey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francis_Allotey "Francis Allotey").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-Allotey_Perspective_on_Ghana-25) After his demise, the center has been organizing summer camps to outreach recently graduated students and motivate them about math, those summer camps are currently named as Allotey Math Summer Camp after him.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-26) A new program to support female students in [STEM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STEM "STEM") has also been launched.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-27)

### Academic programme

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Academic programme")]

The center has two main programs. The general course focused on mathematics and its applications, and AMMI (African Masterd of Machine Intelligence) the course focused on Machine learning patronized by [Google AI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_AI "Google AI"). Moustapha Cisse is the founder and director of AMMI since 2018. The goal of AMMI is to bring the best of AI education in Africa and contribute to building a healthy ecosystem of AI practitioners committed to making a positive impact on our societies.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-28)

Visiting faculty have included, for the main AIMS Master program:[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-AIMS-Ghana-7) Patrick Dorey ([Durham University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durham_University "Durham University")), Barry Green ([Stellenbosch University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stellenbosch_University "Stellenbosch University")), Bernd Schroers ([Heriot-Watt University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heriot-Watt_University "Heriot-Watt University")), [Alessandro Crimi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alessandro_Crimi "Alessandro Crimi") ([University of Zurich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Zurich "University of Zurich")), Bianca Dittrich ([Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perimeter_Institute_for_Theoretical_Physics "Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics")) and others.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-29) While AMMI visiting faculty included Olivier Bousquet ([Google AI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_AI "Google AI")), Hugo Larochelle ([Google AI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_AI "Google AI")), [Yann LeCun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yann_LeCun "Yann LeCun") ([New York University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_University "New York University")), and others.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-30) In both programs each visiting lecturer teaches an intensive three-week-long module.

### Research

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Research")]

Since 2014, AIMS Ghana started conducting research on topics related to applied mathematics and epidemiology. Among the published works, there are the projects of Dr. Olivier Menoukeu Pamen (Alexander Humboldt Chair in Ghana) about [Stochastic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stochastic "Stochastic") Mortality Modelling for Dependent Coupled Lives,[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-Stochastic-31) Dr. Alessandro Crimi about [epidemiological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epidemiology "Epidemiology") study on [prenatal care](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prenatal_care "Prenatal care"),[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-docmeup-32) and during the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic") Esther Opoku Gyasi and Prof. Francis Oduro about cost-effectiveness analysis of COVID-19 data from Ghana.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-covidghana-33)

The **African Institute for Mathematical Sciences** (**AIMS**) is a pan-African network of postgraduate schools teaching mathematical sciences. Established in 2003 in Cape Town, South Africa, AIMS offers postgraduate training, research, and public engagement programs aimed at building scientific capacity across Africa. The institute was founded by physicist [Neil Turok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Turok "Neil Turok") to educate African students in STEM fields to support the continent's development.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-1)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

### Founder

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Founder")]

The first African Institute for Mathematical Sciences was founded in [Muizenberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muizenberg "Muizenberg") near Cape Town by [Neil Turok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Turok "Neil Turok") in 2003, while he was Chair of Mathematical Physics at [Cambridge University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cambridge_University "Cambridge University"). Neil Turok is the son of [Ben Turok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Turok "Ben Turok"), an [ANC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_National_Congress "African National Congress") MP. In 2008 Turok became Executive Director of the [Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perimeter_Institute_for_Theoretical_Physics "Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics"), and was replaced by Dr [Robert Myers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Myers_(physicist) "Robert Myers (physicist)") in 2019.

AIMS South Africa was formed as a partnership between the following universities: [University of Stellenbosch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stellenbosch_University "Stellenbosch University"), [University of Cambridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Cambridge "University of Cambridge"), [University of Cape Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Cape_Town "University of Cape Town"), [University of Oxford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Oxford "University of Oxford"), [University of Paris-Sud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Paris-Sud "University of Paris-Sud"), and [University of the Western Cape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_the_Western_Cape "University of the Western Cape").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-2)

### AIMS Next Einstein Initiative

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: AIMS Next Einstein Initiative")]

AIMS was the subject of a talk[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-3) by [Neil Turok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Turok "Neil Turok") after he received the [TED Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TED_Prize "TED Prize") in 2008.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-4) Neil Turok's TED wish was that, within his lifetime, an African Einstein would be celebrated.

The AIMS Next Einstein Initiative[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-5) is a plan to create 15 more AIMS centres across Africa. These centres intend to create institutions that are equipped with educational and scientific resources equivalent to the more developed continents, in order to fulfil Neil Turok's TED wish.

The first three centres created after that in South Africa are in Senegal,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-6) Ghana[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-AIMS-Ghana-7) and Cameroon. AIMS Senegal became operational in September, 2011 in [Mbour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M'Bour "M'Bour"), near [Dakar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dakar "Dakar"), and AIMS Ghana opened its doors in 2012 in the small coastal city of [Biriwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biriwa "Biriwa"). An earlier centre based at the [African University of Science and Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_University_of_Science_and_Technology "African University of Science and Technology") (AUST[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-8)) in Nigeria was known as AIMS [Abuja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abuja "Abuja")[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-10) for a while. AIMS Ghana was set up in 2012, AIMS [Cameroon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameroon "Cameroon") in 2013 and AIMS [Tanzania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanzania "Tanzania") in 2014. There is a sixth centre in [Rwanda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rwanda "Rwanda").

The AIMS Next Einstein Initiative is a continuation of the work of the African Mathematical Institutes Network (AMI-Net).[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-11)

After AIMS [South Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Africa "South Africa") won the TED Prize in 2008, Neil Turok and his partners developed the AIMS Next Einstein Initiative, the goal of which is to build 15 centres of excellence across [Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Africa "Africa") by 2023. The Government of [Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada "Canada") made a US$20 million investment in the Next Einstein Initiative in 2010, through its [International Development Research Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Development_Research_Centre "International Development Research Centre"), and numerous governments in Africa and Europe have followed suit. In October 2015, a forum took place in [Dakar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dakar "Dakar") under the auspices of UNESCO's International Basic Sciences Programme to take the project for a vast network of centres to the next stage.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-:13-12)

## Mission

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Mission")]

### Teaching and research

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Teaching and research")]

The AIMS institutes teach both basic and applied mathematics, covering a large range of mathematical applications in physics (including astrophysics and cosmology), quantitative biology, [bioinformatics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bioinformatics "Bioinformatics"), scientific computing, finance, agriculture modelling and so on. That in [Senegal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senegal "Senegal") proposes courses in both French and English.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-:13-12) In addition to its academic programmes, AIMS [South Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Africa "South Africa") has a research centre in interdisciplinary areas like cosmology, computing and finance (see below). In 2015, AIMS [Cameroon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameroon "Cameroon") was planning to launch its own research centre to host resident and visiting researchers from universities in [Cameroon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameroon "Cameroon") and beyond.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-:13-12)

### Community service

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Community service")]

The AIMS institutes provide community services. AIMS Senegal has developed an innovative teaching module for secondary school maths teachers and has partnered with local businesses to raise funds for the creation of a national contest on computer applications and mathematical modelling, with a focus on finding development-oriented solutions. AIMS [South Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Africa "South Africa") directs the AIMS Schools Enrichment Centre for primary and secondary school teachers, which also organizes public lectures, workshops and master classes and supports maths clubs in schools across the country (see below). Scholars and lecturers from AIMS Ghana have equipped teachers at [Biriwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biriwa "Biriwa") Junior High School with an innovative teaching module.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-:13-12)

## AIMS South Africa

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: AIMS South Africa")]

### Academic programme

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Academic programme")]

#### Structured Masters programme

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Structured Masters programme")]

The flagship programme of AIMS [South Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Africa "South Africa") is a 10-month Structured Masters programme in the Mathematical Sciences. The programme was upgraded in 2012 from a Postgraduate Diploma. The master's degree is conferred by the three South African universities in the partnership. Students from Africa can apply for full scholarships, including travel, board & lodging, tuition, and a stipend. AIMS is committed to greater participation by women in science and a geographically representative student body from the African continent.

Visiting faculty have included [David MacKay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_J._C._MacKay "David J. C. MacKay"), [Bernt Øksendal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernt_%C3%98ksendal "Bernt Øksendal"), David Aschman ([Cape Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Cape_Town "University of Cape Town")), Alan Beardon ([Cambridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Cambridge "University of Cambridge")), Jordi Campos ([Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Barcelona "University of Barcelona")), Jesus Cerquides ([Spanish National Research Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_National_Research_Council "Spanish National Research Council")), Patrick Dorey ([Durham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durham_University "Durham University")), Pedro Ferreira ([Oxford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxford_University "Oxford University")), Jan Govaerts ([Leuven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katholieke_Universiteit_Leuven "Katholieke Universiteit Leuven")), Barry Green ([Stellenbosch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Stellenbosch "University of Stellenbosch")), Gordon Johnson ([Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Houston "University of Houston")), Dirk Laurie ([Stellenbosch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Stellenbosch "University of Stellenbosch")), Sanjoy Mahajan ([MIT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MIT "MIT"), [Olin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franklin_W._Olin_College_of_Engineering "Franklin W. Olin College of Engineering")), [Vincent Rivasseau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vincent_Rivasseau "Vincent Rivasseau") ([University of Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Paris "University of Paris")), Bernd Schroers ([Heriot-Watt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heriot-Watt_University "Heriot-Watt University")), Robert de Mello Koch ([Witwatersrand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_the_Witwatersrand "University of the Witwatersrand")), Rob Beezer ([University of Puget Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Puget_Sound "University of Puget Sound")), Jeff Sanders ([United Nations University International Institute for Software Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_University_International_Institute_for_Software_Technology "United Nations University International Institute for Software Technology")), and [Tadashi Tokieda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tadashi_Tokieda "Tadashi Tokieda") ([Stanford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanford "Stanford")). Each visiting lecturer teaches an intensive three-week-long module.

The goal of the programme is to produce students capable of doing a high quality research-based master's degree. Special emphasis is placed on intuitive understanding, problem solving skills, collaboration, scientific writing skills, and computer modelling using [Free Software](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_Software "Free Software") such as [SageMath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SageMath "SageMath"), [SciPy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SciPy "SciPy"), and [R](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R_(programming_language) "R (programming language)").

AIMS offers scholarships for many alumni continuing studies in South Africa.

#### Honours Degree in Mathematical Biology

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Honours Degree in Mathematical Biology")]

AIMS, in conjunction with [University of Stellenbosch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stellenbosch_University "Stellenbosch University"), offers an honours degree in [Mathematical Biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematical_and_theoretical_biology "Mathematical and theoretical biology") for South African students.

#### Honours Degree in Mathematical Finance

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Honours Degree in Mathematical Finance")]

An honours degree in [Mathematical Finance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematical_finance "Mathematical finance") is being offered for South African students in conjunction with [University of Stellenbosch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stellenbosch_University "Stellenbosch University") and the [University of Cape Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Cape_Town "University of Cape Town").

#### Master's and doctoral studies

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Master's and doctoral studies")]

In the AIMS Research Centre students, often AIMS alumni, study towards a MSc or PhD degree under supervision of a resident researcher in [Mathematical Biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematical_and_theoretical_biology "Mathematical and theoretical biology") and [Mathematical Finance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematical_finance "Mathematical finance").

### Research centre

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Research centre")]

AIMS [South Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Africa "South Africa") hosts a research centre that opened in May 2008. [Stephen Hawking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Hawking "Stephen Hawking") visited the AIMS research centre and AIMS-Next Einstein Initiative launch.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-14)

The centre specialises in [Mathematical Biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematical_and_theoretical_biology "Mathematical and theoretical biology"), [Industrial Mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Applied_mathematics "Applied mathematics"), [Mathematical Finance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematical_finance "Mathematical finance"), [Astrophysics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astrophysics "Astrophysics")&[Cosmology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physical_cosmology "Physical cosmology"),[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-15) and [Computer Algebra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_algebra_system "Computer algebra system"). Bursaries are offered for Master's and doctoral studies.

### School Enrichment Centre

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: School Enrichment Centre")]

AIMS South Africa hosts a School Enrichment Centre which offers free learning resources and professional development courses for South African mathematics teachers.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-16)

### Workshops and conferences

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Workshops and conferences")]

AIMS South Africa regularly hosts short conferences or workshops in mathematics and its applications, especially in [physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physics "Physics"), [mathematical finance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematical_finance "Mathematical finance"), [epidemiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epidemiology "Epidemiology"). Other topics include [scientific modelling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_modelling "Scientific modelling") or [system administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/System_administration "System administration") using [Debian GNU/Linux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Debian "Debian")[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-17) as a platform.

### Public lectures

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Public lectures")]

Regular public lectures[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-18) on a wide range of topics are offered by [eminent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eminent_domain "Eminent domain") scientists at the forefront of research in their field.

### Funding

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Funding")]

AIMS South Africa is sponsored by international corporations, international development organisations and the South African departments of [Education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Education_(South_Africa) "Department of Education (South Africa)") and [Science and Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Science_and_Technology_(South_Africa) "Department of Science and Technology (South Africa)"). In February 2010, [Google](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google "Google") donated $1 million to AIMS.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-19)

In July 2010, Canada committed CAN$20 million of federal funding to AIMS and the AIMS-Next Einstein Initiative.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-22) The funds are administered by the [International Development Research Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Development_Research_Centre "International Development Research Centre") and the [Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perimeter_Institute_for_Theoretical_Physics "Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics").

In September 2010, the AIMS Next Einstein Initiative AIMS-NEI was awarded US$2 million from [Google](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google "Google")'s Project 10^100.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-23)

Individuals donate to AIMS on GivenGain.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-24)

## AIMS Ghana

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: AIMS Ghana")]

AIMS Ghana is among the oldest AIMS centers.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-AIMS-Ghana-7) Located in West Africa, initially based within the [University of Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Ghana "University of Ghana") in East-Legon, then based in the idyllic village of Biriwa in the Central Region, and then moved to [Accra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accra "Accra"). The center has been highly patronized by the figure of [Francis Allotey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francis_Allotey "Francis Allotey").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-Allotey_Perspective_on_Ghana-25) After his demise, the center has been organizing summer camps to outreach recently graduated students and motivate them about math, those summer camps are currently named as Allotey Math Summer Camp after him.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-26) A new program to support female students in [STEM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STEM "STEM") has also been launched.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-27)

### Academic programme

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Academic programme")]

The center has two main programs. The general course focused on mathematics and its applications, and AMMI (African Masterd of Machine Intelligence) the course focused on Machine learning patronized by [Google AI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_AI "Google AI"). Moustapha Cisse is the founder and director of AMMI since 2018. The goal of AMMI is to bring the best of AI education in Africa and contribute to building a healthy ecosystem of AI practitioners committed to making a positive impact on our societies.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-28)

Visiting faculty have included, for the main AIMS Master program:[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-AIMS-Ghana-7) Patrick Dorey ([Durham University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durham_University "Durham University")), Barry Green ([Stellenbosch University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stellenbosch_University "Stellenbosch University")), Bernd Schroers ([Heriot-Watt University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heriot-Watt_University "Heriot-Watt University")), [Alessandro Crimi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alessandro_Crimi "Alessandro Crimi") ([University of Zurich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Zurich "University of Zurich")), Bianca Dittrich ([Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perimeter_Institute_for_Theoretical_Physics "Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics")) and others.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-29) While AMMI visiting faculty included Olivier Bousquet ([Google AI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_AI "Google AI")), Hugo Larochelle ([Google AI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_AI "Google AI")), [Yann LeCun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yann_LeCun "Yann LeCun") ([New York University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_University "New York University")), and others.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-30) In both programs each visiting lecturer teaches an intensive three-week-long module.

### Research

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Research")]

Since 2014, AIMS Ghana started conducting research on topics related to applied mathematics and epidemiology. Among the published works, there are the projects of Dr. Olivier Menoukeu Pamen (Alexander Humboldt Chair in Ghana) about [Stochastic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stochastic "Stochastic") Mortality Modelling for Dependent Coupled Lives,[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-Stochastic-31) Dr. Alessandro Crimi about [epidemiological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epidemiology "Epidemiology") study on [prenatal care](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prenatal_care "Prenatal care"),[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-docmeup-32) and during the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic") Esther Opoku Gyasi and Prof. Francis Oduro about cost-effectiveness analysis of COVID-19 data from Ghana.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Institute_for_Mathematical_Sciences#cite_note-covidghana-33)
